openings.claim: Small manual taps through an offset head and pin-only guide might align the pin; guide confinement is predicted to limit unintended side force.
openings.discriminator: Alignment without housing contact supports adequacy; housing contact or an immobile pin defeats it. No comparative vibration advantage is predicted.
openings.probe: Proposed only: inspect a surrogate contact envelope, then attempt incremental alignment under varied friction. Housing contact or immobility defeats adequacy.
openings.uncertainty: Guide clearance and required impulse are unknown; no surrogate, equipment, or measurements are supplied.

openings.claim: A controlled powered actuator might reduce operator-dependent pulse variation, improving impulse-size control.
openings.discriminator: Lower pulse variation than manual tapping supports the advantage; equal variation defeats it. Housing-damage reduction is not predicted.
openings.probe: Consider a pulse-variation comparison only after explicit relaxation of manual-only actuation and establishment of an actuator resource.
openings.uncertainty: Currently outside constraints; actuator availability and vibration transmission are unknown.

lineage.reason: Preserves manual pin-only alignment and its contact/immobility adequacy test.
Retained solely as a conditional comparator with its resource and constraint gates explicit.
Lubricant addition violates the constraint. Suggested resistance/impulse reduction, possible ineffectiveness, contamination, and compatibility remain unresolved; no trial within this case.

decision: Prioritize D1 for hypothetical evaluation toward reference-mark alignment without housing damage. Enforce no housing contact, no lubricant addition, and manual actuation only. D2 cannot proceed under current constraints. All proposals are synthetic and untested; unspecified friction and absent equipment prevent any demonstrated feasibility or safety claim.
